findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:0 — evidence mismatch: the missing-intent check in verify-story-review-structured-output.mjs creates a story with no verificationEvidence at all. detectLegacyEvidenceWithoutIntent returns empty, the laneHit branch in story-review.ts (lines 246-254) never fires, and the repairCommand / legacyEvidenceWithoutIntent fields on the issue object are never asserted. The intent claims story_review is tested for evidence-without-intent diagnostics, but the actual test exercises only the plain missing-intent path (no evidence present). The legacy repair-hint wiring through story_review is not integration-tested.

CHK-002:happy:1 — validate-side legacy hint path (decorateStoryVerification in verifier.ts) is not integration-tested. The evidence ref points at verification-intent-repair-smoke.ts, which only calls detectLegacyEvidenceWithoutIntent as a pure function. No test constructs a story with verificationEvidence refs but no verificationIntent, runs lattice validate against it, and asserts (a) the result is still failing and (b) the legacyEvidenceWithoutIntent hint with the repair command appears in details/legacyEvidenceWithoutIntent response fields. The validate-side wiring added in verifier.ts lines 338-383 has no end-to-end smoke coverage.

CHK-002:adversarial:0 — no integration test confirms that when story_review or validate processes a story with evidence-without-intent, the issued diagnostic retains severity=blocker and does not downgrade. The evidence ref points at verification-intent-repair-smoke.ts, which only tests the pure detector function. The no-downgrade guarantee is only enforced by reading the source code of story-review.ts (line 248: severity:blocker is hardcoded), not by a live CLI call. This is advisory: the code path is visually correct, but the behavioral contract is not regression-protected by an executable assertion.

quality-cleanup: checklist.ts:202 dead-code guard `m[1] !== item.id` in reconstructMissingIntentsFromEvidence — the startsWith(`${item.id}:`) check on line 197 already guarantees m[1]===item.id after the regex matches; the continue on line 202 is unreachable and creates misleading code suggesting a cross-item scenario that cannot occur given the preceding guard
